minimum_events: Password resets; unlocks; MFA factor changes; device registration; role changes; token issuance; session revocation
primary_questions: Who changed the account; which factor or device appeared; what was accessed afterwards
financial_use_cases: Help-desk compromise; token phishing; valid accounts; BEC
retention_note: Retain long enough to investigate activity preceding data theft or payment changes

minimum_events: Tickets; call records; verification method; override actions; customer record views; operator and supplier identity
primary_questions: Was the caller verified; did access match a valid case; did an operator exceed normal scope
financial_use_cases: Scattered Spider; support-insider fraud; customer impersonation
retention_note: Retention must support insider and customer-fraud investigations and comply with privacy law
owner_examples: Service desk; customer support; insider risk; legal

minimum_events: Full headers; gateway verdicts; mailbox sign-ins; forwarding rules; delegation; OAuth grants; mail and file access
primary_questions: Was a sender spoofed or mailbox compromised; were finance conversations read; did token access occur
financial_use_cases: BEC; Kali365; internal phishing; SaaS theft
retention_note: Cloud audit defaults may be shorter than the incident-discovery period

minimum_events: Process and command line; script interpreters; package installs; containers; file and credential access; DNS and network
primary_questions: What code ran; did a package spawn a shell; were secrets accessed
financial_use_cases: UNC1069; UNC4899; DMM Bitcoin; malicious attachments; ClickFix
retention_note: Developer and macOS/Linux telemetry should be retained alongside Windows data

minimum_events: Repository logins; token creation; permission changes; dependency and lockfile changes; pipeline jobs; artifact hashes; package publishing
primary_questions: Who changed the dependency; which build and customers received it
financial_use_cases: Axios supply chain; APT41 supply chain; transaction software compromise
retention_note: Preserve build provenance and package metadata across release lifecycles

minimum_events: Control-plane API calls; object access; application grants; service principals; storage sharing; sync jobs; cloud network and bastion access
primary_questions: Did a new identity assign access; was data moved cloud-to-cloud; were transaction systems reached
financial_use_cases: Scattered Spider; APT41 DUST; DPRK cloud theft; token phishing
retention_note: Retain control-plane and data-plane logs; both may be required

minimum_events: Asset/version inventory; WAF; reverse proxy; application and database logs; file integrity; application accounts; outbound traffic
primary_questions: Which request preceded file creation; did the web process launch a shell; what data was exported
financial_use_cases: MOVEit; Oracle EBS; APT41; zero-day exploitation
retention_note: Keep history predating patch or extortion contact

minimum_events: Beneficiary changes; supplier master; payment approvals; transaction amount/country/destination; recall and freeze actions; wallet addresses
primary_questions: Did a suspicious email or identity event precede payment; where did funds move
financial_use_cases: BEC; DPRK theft; Cobalt; Silence; customer fraud
retention_note: Financial and cyber timelines must be correlatable

minimum_events: Hypervisor logins; role changes; ISO mounts; VM shutdown/export/deletion; backup policy and deletion; recovery tests
primary_questions: Did a newly changed admin affect many systems; can recovery still be trusted
retention_note: Retain management-plane logs outside the environment they protect

minimum_events: Flow; bandwidth; requests; CDN/WAF/scrubbing; DNS health; load balancer; application latency/errors; transaction success
primary_questions: Is traffic malicious; which service failed; what customer impact occurred
retention_note: Store summary and incident packet or request evidence proportionately

minimum_events: Service inventory; data and access scope; supplier contacts; subcontractors; notifications; audit evidence; exit plans
primary_questions: Which service depends on the supplier; what evidence can it provide; can it be replaced
financial_use_cases: MOVEit; Oracle EBS; DMM supplier; Coinbase support; DORA
retention_note: Contractual evidence and dependency history may need multi-year retention
owner_examples: Procurement; third-party risk; legal; business owner; SOC
